answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 III cards and use all at the bottom; shuffle 9 II and deal 5 above them; shuffle 3 I and deal 1 on top. Return unused I and II unseen to the box.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle the four Conflict III cards… Shuffle the nine Conflict II… deal five… Shuffle the three Conflict I… deal one’; unused cards returned without looking.

answers.answer: Both have 3 Agents (2 on Leader, third Swordmaster beside board), 12 troops (3 in garrison and 9 in supply), and 1 water. Four-player human starts at 1 VP; three-player starts at 0 VP.
answers.evidence: Setup 6: Score track on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third next to board; 12 troops; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you, from both Agent and Reveal turns, go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Reveal Turn: may Reveal while Agents remain; after Reveal turns are skipped; resolve Reveal boxes of just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front to discard.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent can pay the entry cost, if available before entry. Resources gained only after placement from the destination or the played Agent card cannot pay that same cost. One card sends only one Agent, using only one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; reveal it on Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot may be played before placing Agent and grants before entry count; post-placement gains cannot pay. Agent Turn: choose only one icon; no-icon card only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space deploy all three troops recruited during this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for up to five. At a non-Combat space, you do not deploy troops. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before any deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: cube recruits from supply to garrison; at Combat space deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: Spy Agent icon allows sending an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that Spy stays there. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player, bypassing their Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both; on placement, choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent, before any space or card effects.
answers.evidence: Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence draws after Agent placement and before effects; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops ×2, one sandworm ×3, and four swords ×1. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. A player with no unit cannot play Combat Intrigue, since only a player with at least one unit in the Conflict participates.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; if last unit removed strength 0. Combat Intrigue: players with at least one unit in Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. You may act again after passing if another player plays; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply, sandworms to bank, markers reset.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in four-player play, each receives the second reward; the other players compete for the third reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In three-player play, each tied player takes second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first with 4 players leaves remaining players competing for third; with 3 or fewer no other rewards; no one takes card. Combat rules: 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional cost reward, you may pay a second time to get it again: for a 3-spice-for-1-VP option, pay 3 more spice for another VP, or 6 total spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; location control and Conflict battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid again (3 spice for 1 VP example).

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check for a same-icon face-up Conflict or Objective there; if matched, you must flip the pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: check after taking won card; face-up Conflict or Objective; must flip pair; Endgame wild can match any icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP; lose that VP below 2 and regain on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. First to 4 also gets Alliance and 1 VP, which stays only while holding it. Tying the holder does not take it; rise above the holder to transfer it (with FAQ exception for holder losing Influence after a tie).
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP reversible; separate 4 Influence track bonus retained; first to 4 gets Alliance VP; tying does not steal, rising above transfers.

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled across sources for one purchase or split across multiple cards. You may buy a Row replacement immediately if able. Buy Row cards or either Reserve card, at the cost shown top right; acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: acquire during Reveal; pool/split Persuasion; replace Row to five, can acquire replacement; cost top right; acquired card face up in discard.

answers.answer: At a Maker space without an Agent, add one spice during Makers; visiting collects all bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. A worm cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while Shield Wall remains. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A worm is deployed directly into the Conflict, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Board Space Guide; Sandworms: bonus spice, costs/options, protected Conflicts, Hooks not universal and never spent; worm immediately deployed, never garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, after a round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops, in that order.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: at end of round trigger; Endgame Intrigue before winner; tie order spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Shuffle 20 standard contracts; flip 2 face up below the Landsraad Council and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 extra Intrigue and 4 extra Imperium cards into their decks. Shaddam is an optional Leader choice. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Components specify 20 standard plus 10 Rise of Ix compatibility tokens; separate set left in box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, contract icon lets you take one of two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank token flipped face up. If none remain, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the contract’s shown spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts define each completion condition and fallback.

answers.answer: No. If you take a space contract after already sending an Agent there this turn, completion waits until a future turn; you must hold it when you send the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: must have contract at time Agent sent; announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective. First Player goes to the human whose Objective shows it; First Player alternates only between humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival setup: one shared scoring Rival, Ornithopter Objective, First Player assigned to human; Rival immediately clockwise; never Reveals.

answers.answer: Ignore occupied destinations and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an eligible empty post if possible, but never places an Agent; either way reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore normal board-space costs/effects and apply only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: skip occupied; Place Spy does not place Agent, draw another; ignore normal costs/effects; reshuffle if empty or Reshuffle.

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, remove Objective cards whose marking does not match player count, shuffle eligible cards, and give one face up to each player; the card showing First Player marker determines first player. Shaddam may be used only with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objective cards, shuffle and distribute face up; marked Objective determines First Player. Shaddam is not used unless CHOAM.

answers.answer: Bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if exhausted. By contrast, if your troop supply is empty you cannot recruit more until troops return to it. Gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: resources/sandworms not limited, substitute if run out; gains from bank, payments returned. Recruiting: cannot recruit if supply empty.

answers.answer: Phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal and place the Conflict first, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise, and start next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists phase order; Round Start reveals Conflict, defensive bonus, then draw five; Recall prepares next round.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space, Agent-box, and Influence effects may be carried out in any order after entry, but entry costs and requirements must be met immediately before resolving any space or played-card effects. Thus the visit’s Influence cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before resolving effects; after that, space and Agent box and Faction advance may be in any order.

answers.answer: Normally an optional arrow cost/effect can be paid only once per turn; you cannot pay twice for the same effect. Sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card/space effects are mandatory; ‘may,’ optional arrows, and black-X trash are optional, but direct trash instructions and Intrigue costs/conditions are mandatory.
answers.evidence: Arrows: effect once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ: most effects mandatory; exceptions listed; direct trash mandatory; Intrigue costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of yours for no effect. If the placement effect specifies a connected Agent-icon type, the post must be connected to a space of that type or you cannot place it.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post; may recall if no Spy in supply; specified Agent icon must connect to post.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent; it bypasses another player’s. A Spy recall does not replace the card/Agent turn requirement. You may recall two Spies for different effects, one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence, but never two for Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spy rules; FAQ: recalling Spy still requires card Agent turn; may recall two for different effects, never two to Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller receives the location bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin; the visitor also gets that space’s own effects. Winning its named Conflict puts your Control marker there, replacing opponent’s marker. On revealing that Conflict, existing controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: location bonuses and replacement on winning; defensive bonus on reveal, troop from supply.

answers.answer: Tie for second: each tied player gets the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and Conflict card, with no further rewards. Tie for third: tied players get nothing. Three-way tie for first: each gets second reward; no further rewards and nobody takes the card, in either 3- or 4-player play.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and tie table: second, third, and three tied first rules.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive ordinary rewards; third gets nothing. The same ranks apply in a two-human game with Rival: Rival counts as a player, so 2–3-player reward rules apply.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 2 or 3 players including Rival pay first and second; ordinary third gets nothing except tie for second.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from deck; after resolving, place face up in discard beside Intrigue Deck. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards and FAQ Draw timing: types/timing, keep separate face down, resolved to discard, reshuffle discard if deck runs out.

answers.answer: Ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from hand. Secrets takes one Intrigue at random from each opponent with four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Special Rules: Intrigue trash icon; Secrets opponent threshold and random selection.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary cards to box; Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or the card directs itself to be trashed. The Spice Must Flow’s acquired VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory: Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if later trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effect happens once when acquiring the card. If unable to draw because deck is empty, shuffle discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at end of Reveal.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: deck reshuffle and Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns or revealed on Reveal remain face up and in play through Clean Up unless trashed first. Fremen Bond uses one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order played. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond section.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just placed; it can be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops: retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain-two Influence effect chooses one Faction only; it cannot split across two. Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with the specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: gain two with free choice cannot choose two factions; Alliance icon requires token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; when several were tied, former holder chooses the recipient. If holder falls to 3 or lower and no one has 4+, return token to board and former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss; Influence scoring details.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed and used immediately this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, which then adds to the five drawn cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal immediate; after Reveal next round; Plot with later Reveal effect stays face up until then.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because no one wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it can be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play after tie for first; if received as winning reward can play immediately.

answers.answer: If all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores can exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: all four tiebreakers tied → most recent Reveal; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. Complete all contracts you hold for that same space with one Agent placement, provided you held them when placing the Agent. Contract reward is another effect of the Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; effects resolve in any order; must hold at placement.

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts. His Sardaukar Commander ability lets him choose one of those when acquiring a contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent and lasts only that turn, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam clarifications.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost Training track space and remains on the rightmost once it reaches it. Begin with Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2; reaching 2 can trigger again after losing Influence and regaining it, but moving down through 2 is not reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan reach; Spacing Guild’s Favor. FAQ Jessica-related details.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, always draws one card, and with CHOAM takes a contract or otherwise gives 2 Solari. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, has no cost, gives 1 Emperor Influence, and likewise takes a contract with CHOAM or gives 2 Solari without it. Neither is a Faction Agent space, so neither automatically gives Influence merely for visiting; Dutiful’s listed Influence is explicit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Accept Contract and Dutiful Service; guide explains only Faction spaces grant automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Visiting either gains all accumulated bonus spice even if choosing worms; Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Deep Desert/Hagga; Sandworm Reward rules say gain all bonus spice; Hooks retained.

answers.answer: Both require City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, and no resource cost. One option takes Hooks if lacking, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. The other gains 1 water and optionally removes Shield Wall; it does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row lists both options and no resource cost.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access and costs 5 Solari each visit; it is not a Combat space. First visit places Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal for rest of game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one, then 6 Solari. Each player may take it only once. The third Agent is available the same round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also reduces human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Effects: may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically advance Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; Landsraad is not Faction and has only explicitly listed Influence effects.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and gains 5 Solari plus 1 Influence with any one Faction. That free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, non-Combat: choose 0 or pay 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if paying also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat: choose 0 or pay 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 if paying; controller gains 1 Solari either way.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner: cost 5 spice, gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit five; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: cost 1 water, gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit one, optionally trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: cost 4 spice, gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall (Landsraad, no cost, non-Combat) draws an Intrigue and grants 1 Persuasion during your Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage (Bene Gesserit, 1 spice, non-Combat) gains 1 BG Influence, draws a card, places a Spy. Deliver Supplies (Guild, no cost, non-Combat) gains 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. During Reveal, ignore Litany Against Fear’s red box, or ignore it when gaining an Agent icon and playing normally as Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ final clarifications: False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without its 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: Rival setup: color, four cubes at bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside board, three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Rival can win; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall like a human.
answers.evidence: Required Rival setup and turn rules.

answers.answer: As soon as its count of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water reaches the printed Swordmaster threshold, spend that many and take third Agent for current round. Count each item as one; spend Solari, spice, Intrigue, then water; retain leftovers. The new Agent is usable immediately this round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each exact set: 7 Solari, or 7 spice, or 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP each. It cannot combine mixed resources into a set of seven.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains/losses 2-Influence VP and Alliances like human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Influence; numbered icon explanation.

answers.answer: No. Choose only the destination matching current conditions; if occupied, reveal another card without using the other destination. Guild Influence determines Accept Contract/Shipping choice; Conflict tier determines Deliver Supplies/Heighliner choice.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination selection conditions and occupied destination handling.

answers.answer: At every Rival Combat space, deploy up to two available garrison troops even if card recruited none; newly recruited troops also deploy there. Troop icons at noncombat spaces put recruits in garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus that is unmet is simply omitted and does not prevent Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: deploy up to two at every Combat space; noncombat recruits to garrison; missing conditional bonus does not prevent placement.

answers.answer: For unspecified post type, choose first available Faction observation post by priority; if all four occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers Scheme. Rival never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If Scheme recruits before placement and Rival then visits Combat space that turn, deploy those recruits too. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Rival Agent turns Place Spy handling.

answers.answer: At Hagga/Deep Desert with Hooks and a Conflict allowing worms, Rival summons one/two worms instead of base spice; without Hooks or if protected, it summons none and takes base spice (2/4). It always takes all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: choices, protected Conflict implication, base spice, bonus spice.

answers.answer: At beginning of Combat, if Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section.

answers.answer: Yes, Rival gets control bonuses on visits, defensive troop on reveal if it controls space, battle-icon VP, and sandworm reward doubling. It always takes optional Conflict VP if able to pay or recall needed Spies. With CHOAM it never takes contracts; contract reward gives 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat and CHOAM rules.

answers.answer: Set and announce total strength at any point while resolving Reveal effects, updating as needed during the Reveal turn. For strength over 20, flip Combat marker to +20 and start again from beginning of track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn strength timing; Strength: over 20 marker procedure.

answers.answer: Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not merely revealing it. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities and Overview: any type of card can override usual rules.

answers.answer: Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recall uses without a card.
answers.evidence: Spies: Recall Spy icon and two recall effects without a card.

answers.answer: Trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Ordinary discard selects a card from your hand but cannot select an Intrigue unless specified; it does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: A doubled reward that grants one Influence of your choice can grant it twice, choosing the same Faction or two different Factions. A single effect granting two free-choice Influence must choose only one Faction for both.
answers.evidence: Sandworm doubling example gives 2 Influence with same or two different Factions; Influence rule says gain-two free choice cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival’s printed Signet Ring ability shown by its Rival card. The Hagal card itself supplies the trigger; the Rival does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules say follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; summary does not state a separate timing/trigger for the Hagal Signet Ring icon.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks icon takes a token if Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, take no extra. Shield Wall removal works only if Rival has Hooks and Wall remains; otherwise ignore it. Removal returns Wall to box permanently.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table; Shield Wall rule says cannot return.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing, and is non-Combat. It grants 1 BG Influence and draws one Intrigue from the deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row and Intrigue rules.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, costs nothing, and is Combat. Visitor gets 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there; controller gains 1 spice. If visitor controls it, that player receives both its visitor effects and controller bonus.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; guide says resolve visitor and controller bonuses even when same player.

answers.answer: Reveal new Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from earlier rounds; those remain. Then resolve defensive bonus, then each player draws five cards.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal new Conflict, place atop remaining old cards, defensive bonus, then draw five.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube at the bottom of each of four Faction Influence tracks. Alliance tokens start on marked areas of those tracks, so no player starts holding one. Shield Wall token starts below Spice Refinery on the board.
answers.evidence: Setup 1 and 6.

answers.answer: First Player begins, then play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Revealed players are skipped thereafter; in standard 3–4-player play Player Turns end when all have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, First Player starts and priority continues clockwise; each eligible player may play any number or pass, and a prior pass does not prevent acting later.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Combat Intrigue rules.

answers.answer: Steps: Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand); Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve just-revealed cards, acquire with Persuasion, set strength); Clean Up (move all cards in front to discard). Reveal effects can be resolved in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn three steps; resolve Reveal effects in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starter face down and place to left of Leader. Without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards from Intrigue and Imperium decks; shuffle separately face down; deal 5 Imperium cards face up to Row; put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; 3 Spies in supply; Councilor in supply; Control markers in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup 4 and 6; Initial card states table; components/setup.

answers.answer: During Reveal turn, ordinary purchases are any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card (Prepare the Way, The Spice Must Flow). Cost appears at top right of card. They may be acquired using Persuasion during Reveal only.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards section.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even if legal; declining a recall used as cost also declines its benefit. Shield Wall detonation icon allows removal, so it is optional. Once removed, Wall stays gone for rest of game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: placement/recall optional; Shield Wall removal and no return.

answers.answer: Normally a played card’s Agent icon must match the destination access icon. A Spy merely connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. If the card has Spy Agent icon, it can access a board space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn card icon requirement; Spy Agent icon section.

answers.answer: Yes, first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing Agent; its resources gained before entry can pay. Resources from the Agent card or destination arise only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns timing of Plot Intrigue and entry costs.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, skip humans who Revealed but continue Rival’s Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and Rival used all Agents. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player exception.

answers.answer: Standard board space access / Combat: Accept Contract—Spice Trade/no; Arrakeen—City/yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad/no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade/yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild/no; Desert Tactics—Fremen/yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor/no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit/no; Fremkit—Fremen/yes; Gather Support—Landsraad/no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade/yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild/yes; High Council—Landsraad/no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade/yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad/no; Research Station—City/yes; Sardaukar—Emperor/no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit/no; Shipping—Spice Trade/no; Sietch Tabr—City/yes; Spice Refinery—City/yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad/no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists all 22 spaces with access and Combat? columns.

answers.answer: When the Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to Conflict, without an Agent visit. After rewards, reset all Combat markers to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive troop bonus; Combat cleanup resets markers.

answers.answer: Play a card from your hand face up in front of you and send an Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve its Agent box, not Reveal box; destination effects also resolve. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile, or simply move an Agent already on board; a new Agent turn uses a card from hand and an Agent from Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn rules; Reveal turn separates cards played Agent and revealed; Recall Agent is separate effect.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Signet Ring is played to send the Agent; Shaddam cannot defer it by resolving space effects first.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately; freedom to order effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: In four-player play, first, second, and third place get their printed rewards; fourth gets none. Highest-strength winner takes the Conflict card and then checks for a mandatory battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat player-count rewards; winner takes card and checks battle-icon pair.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random.
answers.evidence: Setup 3: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: Ordinary draw-a-card comes from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile if necessary; you cannot choose a card directly from discard. Intrigue draw icon draws from Intrigue Deck instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards section.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival; retain the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A later acquired token moves from bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup 7 Maker Hooks tokens.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes units or strength, adjust the Combat marker when that card resolves during Combat Intrigue window. Rewards use the adjusted strength shown on track, not a fixed Reveal value.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: adjust marker when card resolves; resolve using adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Gains of Solari, spice, or water come from the bank; another player’s supply is not the source. Payments return resources to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: resource gains from bank, payments return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down, then flip two face up as offers and put remaining 18 face down in bank. Players do not choose offers or preset the order; shuffle randomizes them.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle 20 contracts face down, flip two, remaining 18 face down in bank.
